category_specific_evidence: Issue #40342: jax.grad(jax.nn.sigmoid) returns 0.0 at x=40.0 in float64 where expected derivative is 4.248354255291589e-18; the default public API loses this finite tail derivative.
Negative-side derivative at x=-40.0 is retained (4.24835425529159e-18), so the result is not underflow.
lax.logistic with accuracy=lax.AccuracyMode.HIGHEST returns the expected nonzero derivative at x=40.0, showing a stable derivative path exists.
PR#30346: sigmoid derivative sigmoid(x)*(1-sigmoid(x)) is inaccurate near 1 and caused gradient to vanish for x > ~17 although it should vanish only at ~88.
PR#30346: the fix uses sigmoid(x)*sigmoid(-x) for sigmoid, exp(x) for expm1 derivative (replacing expm1(x)+1, inaccurate for large negative x), and 4*sigmoid(2x)*sigmoid(-2x) for tanh.
PR#30346 notes changes modify behavior only when accuracy is HIGHEST, due to performance concerns.

Diff to lax.py changes expm1 JVP to use exp(x, accuracy=accuracy) when accuracy is HIGHEST; the test diff adds testExpm1Grad over x in [-80, 80) in float32 and testEvenFunctionGrads for logistic and tanh over x in [0, 80) in float32.
Issue discussion: keeping the more accurate implementation behind the non-default flag because the HIGHEST path is potentially slower for a commonly-used function.
reproduction_risks: Default-accuracy path returns 0.0 at x=40 in float64, so reproduction must use float64 with jax_enable_x64 enabled and compare default vs AccuracyMode.HIGHEST.
The expected value 4.248354255291589e-18 is a tiny magnitude; a loose tolerance could mask the zero-versus-nonzero discrepancy.
Passages' float32 tolerance tests do not establish the float64 separation tolerance; the float64 tolerance is not stated.
